newsitem.title: USA: Ford trims Q4 North American output forecast.
newsitem.headline: Ford trims Q4 North American output forecast.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday it lowered its North American fourth quarter vehicle output forecast by 30,000 units to 1,045,000 to adjust for production losses.
The new number is still above the 1,014,000 units it made in the fourth quarter of 1995.

Ford spokesman Joel Pitcoff said the revised forecast reflects component shortages in the U.S., including V-8 engines, that held back production of several car lines -- Thunderbirds, Cougars, Mustangs, Crown Victorias and Grand Marquis -- and Econoline vans.
The engine shortage has also forced Ford to cut back on some light truck overtime, he said. Of the 30,000 unit change, 17,000 units were lost in October.
"Fundamentally, there's no change in the outlook on the market. This is just a reflection of an inability to produce as much as we had intended," he said.

Salomon Bros analyst Jack Kirnan said Ford's worldwide production schedule for the fourth quarter is down a total of 20,000 units. That is because Ford added 10,000 units of production of its Fiesta overseas.
Kirnan noted the Mustang, Probe and Thunderbird/Cougar cars affected by the cutbacks are the weaker part of Ford's passenger car operations.
